what_its_for: Econazole nitrate is an antifungal cream used to treat fungal skin infections. These include athlete's foot (tinea pedis), jock itch (tinea cruris), ringworm (tinea corporis), and a skin condition called tinea versicolor, which causes patches of lighter or darker skin. It works by stopping the growth of the fungus causing your infection.
how_to_take: This medicine is applied directly to your skin. Before applying, clean and dry the affected area completely. Using your fingertips, spread a thin layer of the cream over the infected skin and a small area around it. Rub it in gently. Wash your hands thoroughly after applying unless you are treating your hands. Do not put this cream in your eyes, mouth, or vagina. Do not bandage the area tightly unless your doctor tells you to.
dosing: For most fungal infections such as ringworm and jock itch, apply the cream once a day, usually at bedtime. For athlete's foot, apply the cream twice a day, in the morning and at night. Always follow the exact directions given by your doctor or pharmacist. Keep using the cream for the full amount of time your doctor prescribed, even if your skin looks better before you finish. Stopping too soon can let the infection come back.
missed_dose: If you forget to apply a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular routine. Do not apply extra cream to make up for a missed application.
storage: Store this cream at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat and direct sunlight. Keep the tube tightly closed when you are not using it. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not freeze the cream.
what_to_avoid: Do not use this cream near your eyes, nose, or mouth. Avoid getting the cream inside your vagina. Do not wrap the treated area tightly with bandages or plastic wrap unless your doctor tells you to, as this can increase absorption and cause unwanted side effects. Avoid sharing towels, clothing, or shoes while you have an active infection, as fungal infections can spread to other people. Keep the affected area as clean and dry as possible.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor if your skin becomes more red, swollen, blistered, or irritated after starting this cream. Call your doctor if you develop a rash, hives, or have trouble breathing, as these could be signs of an allergic reaction. Also call your doctor if your infection does not start to improve after 2 weeks of treatment, or if it comes back after you finish treatment. Seek emergency help right away if you have severe swelling of the face, throat, or tongue.
when_it_works: You may start to feel some relief, such as less itching or burning, within the first few days of use. However, the full benefit of the medicine takes longer. Most infections clear up within 2 to 4 weeks, but athlete's foot may take up to 4 weeks. It is very important to keep using the cream for the entire length of time prescribed, even if your symptoms go away sooner, to make sure the infection is completely gone.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding women should talk to their doctor before using this cream. While it is generally considered low-risk when used on the skin, your doctor should approve its use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. This cream is generally safe for use in children, but always follow your doctor's specific instructions for dosing in children. Older adults can typically use this cream the same way as other adults. If you have sensitive skin or a history of skin allergies, let your doctor know before starting this medicine.
